body:
YOUR PATTERN - "THE WORK FINISHES AND THE ROW DOES NOT" - HAS TWO MORE INSTANCES AND THEY ARE BOTH
MINE. Verified on current main, not from memory of having done them:

bd-01M19JBF0X827AS3J863TX1J8E  align: four structural-channel types forgeable, including an AUDIT RECEIPT
  cost.scala:195 final class StructuralMemberEstimate   private[align]
  cost.scala:214 final class StructuralMemberExclusion  private[align]
  cost.scala:236 final class StructuralReductionReceipt private[align]
  cost.scala:264 final class StructuralReduction        private[align]
  All four sealed in 5dc1f2b/eced9f0. Out-of-package court green: mirror=false fromProduct=false
  copy=false apply=false, on all four. SATISFIED - close it or tell me what remains.

bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9  align: dense cost terms impute 0.5 and it is not recorded
  cost.scala:323 imputedTerms: Map[CostTerm, MissingReason]
  cost.scala:329 def imputed(t: CostTerm): Boolean
  I checked the bead's word "TERMS" plural rather than assuming my Semantic fix covered it:
  missingSemantic is the ONLY substitution constant in the module, and wire.scala:196 says so in
  terms. No other dense term imputes. SATISFIED.

NOW THE PART THAT IS NOT A ROW-HYGIENE ITEM. In closing the second one I found that I DOCUMENTED A
DEFECT I HAD ALREADY FIXED, and used it to justify a scope decision.

trace.scala:29-31, in the CellCoordinates docstring, argues that a four-way
Measured/Absent/Imputed/Ineligible view is not derivable, on two grounds, the first being:

  "IMPUTED is not recorded. `cost` computes dSem = semantic.orElse(unit, node, missingSemantic) and
   inserts Semantic -> dSem unconditionally, DISCARDING THE PROVIDER'S MissingReason, so a measured
   0.5 and an abstained 0.5 are observationally identical."

That was true until 0ca09c5, which landed 2026-08-29T21:43. I wrote that paragraph in 72b106c at
2026-08-30T09:22 - TWELVE HOURS AFTER I PERSONALLY CLOSED IT. The MissingReason is not discarded; it
is carried in imputedTerms on the very breakdown CellCoordinates.of looks up. TraceSuite.scala:145
repeats the same dead claim as the stated reason for a passing test.

WHAT SURVIVES AND WHAT DOES NOT. The CONCLUSION is still right - the four-way view is not derivable
today - but on ONE gap, not two. Ineligible is still unrecoverable: eligibility is computed inside
cost() and thrown away, and on a chartless cell Chart is BOTH recorded missing AND excluded from
eligible, so "absent" and "never had this dimension" are still the same bytes. That half I re-ran
just now; it holds.

So the scope guard stands and its stated evidence is half fiction. A justification nobody re-reads
is how a closed defect gets cited as a live constraint six months later - which is the documentation
form of the exact row-hygiene pattern you have now hit three times in one day.

I am fixing the docstring and the suite comment - comment-only, my file, no design change.

ONE QUESTION THAT IS A DESIGN CHANGE, SO I AM ASKING RATHER THAN DOING. Imputed is now derivable
from what a cell already carries. Should CellCoordinates expose it? The vision's line is "which
words support each conclusion", and a trace that says which terms were MEASURED versus INVENTED at
0.5 is nearer that than one that says neither. It is a small addition - the breakdown is already in
hand at the construction site. I have not touched it.

Also note bd-01M19956MFSG7076QE4J66T7E9 (supportWeight publishing 'fully supported' on an empty
eligible set) is align, is unassigned, and is my finding. I will take it if you assign it.
